heading: File names follow the class
body:
Every class file is named after its one class, as in Java. The file name without the extension is the class name, with the same spelling and the same capital letters. This rule is the same in every language, both in client/ and in server/: `client/services/CartService.ts` holds `CartService`, `server/models/Order.py` holds `Order`, `server/models/Order.rb` holds `Order = Data.define(...)`, and `client/tests/CartServiceTest.go` holds `type CartServiceTest struct`. It covers role files, models, test units, test setups, utilities, error types and every other file in client/ or server/ that declares a class, a struct, a record or another type. A models file holds one model, and it is named after that model. A models file with a second model, for example `Order.ts` with `Order` and `Status`, also fails with `TY1318`. Some files keep the name that Tachyon gives them: views and component files (`tac.html` and its `tac.*` companions) in client/pages/ and client/components/, plain code in client/shared/ and server/shared/, workers in server/workers/ (their class is `Handler`), and the root `middleware.<ext>` file (its class is `Middleware`). A file that declares no type, such as a Python script with functions only, has no class to follow.

A file with another name fails with `TY1318` before the app runs. The message names both fixes: rename the file after the class, or rename the class after the file. `ty migrate fix --write` renames the file when it declares exactly one type. It splits a models file with several models into one file per model: each new file keeps the imports and the comments of its model, and the files that import a moved TypeScript or Dart model import it from its new file. When other files use the old file name, for example in a relay command, it renames the class instead, or lists a manual step (ADR 0067).
